content.text:
**p30:** Using Chinook now, in response to Redoer's attach, is clearly right. Redoer has no materials at this moment, so it can't answer Chinook by banishing itself or by putting my Black-Winged Dragon back on top of my Deck. Chinook resolves first, which negates Redoer, so the attach does nothing. Redoer then sits at 1700 ATK for Black-Winged Dragon (2800) to destroy in battle. Time Thief Retrograde only negates Spells and Traps, so it can't stop Chinook. Passing lets Redoer pick up a material and its protection.

**p22:** Stealing Blue-Eyes Alternative with Enemy Controller (Tributing Ahrima) deals 3000 damage. It also leaves my board empty for a Simoon turn next time, and Chinook stays in hand as Simoon's banish cost. Setting Enemy Controller has some defensive value on their turn, but it gives up 3000 damage and Ahrima probably dies either way.

**p27:** The opponent's board is empty, and 9000 ATK of attackers against 5200 LP is lethal. Which attacker goes first barely matters.

Chinook resolves first, which negates Redoer: the attach does nothing and Redoer can't use its Quick Effect this turn. Redoer drops to 1700, so Black-Winged Dragon kills it in battle. Retrograde can't stop a monster effect. Passing lets Redoer gain a material and the protection that comes with it.

grades.reason: Passing gives Redoer a material, so it can later dodge Chinook or spin Black-Winged Dragon back to the Deck. Right now it is the 'real threat' and it has no protection.

Setting Enemy Controller for their turn has some defensive value, but it gives up the damage, Ahrima likely dies anyway, and the Set card can be banished.
